checkpoints.claim_or_design: The existing adversarial review validator safely prevents publication records from authorizing protected experiments or weak evidence.
checkpoints.challenge_method: Construct counterexamples using normalized variants of protected scopes and unstructured commit-evidence labels.
findings: Version 1 compares forbidden experiment scopes by exact string equality, permitting variants such as production_deployment, Live-DNS, and mixed-case forms.
Version 1 accepts any nonempty commit_matched_evidence array, including an unstructured passed label that proves no commit binding.
repairs: Selected an additive version 2 validator so existing version 1 consumers are not silently broken.
Defined normalized protected-token matching and structured exact-commit evidence requirements.
remaining_uncertainty: Repository-wide version 1 consumer inventory is incomplete.
No runtime test execution evidence exists for version 2.
evidence_required_before_publication: Commit-bound preview and accessibility evidence for any public artifact
checkpoints.next_falsifiable_step: Execute the version 2 Node suite at its exact commit and retain the output.

checkpoints.claim_or_design: Version 2 closes the identified bypasses without touching protected runtime surfaces.
checkpoints.challenge_method: Add reversible negative fixtures for scope separator variants, case variation, mismatched commits, unstructured evidence, malformed findings, and a permitted disposable fixture.
findings: Protected-scope matching now normalizes underscores, slashes, dots, backslashes, hyphens, case, and repeated whitespace.
Publication evidence now requires commit_sha, locator, claim, and observed_at, with commit_sha equal to artifact_commit.
The experiments are source fixtures only and do not mutate deployments, schedules, automations, shared state, DNS, credentials, or user data.
repairs: Added normalized substring guards for protected scope families.
Added typed string-array validation for findings, repairs, evidence, and uncertainty.
remaining_uncertainty: Substring protection may conservatively reject a benign fixture name containing a protected token.
The suite is committed but not executed through the connector.
evidence_required_before_publication: A deliberate benign-token false-positive fixture to calibrate protection breadth
checkpoints.next_falsifiable_step: Test whether a benign scope containing a protected word is rejected too broadly and refine with explicit namespaces if necessary.

checkpoints.claim_or_design: The implementation is verified and ready to become the publication gate.
checkpoints.challenge_method: Separate source existence, test design, runtime test passage, integration, preview behavior, accessibility, and publication readiness into independent claims.
evidence: GitHub commits for source and test files
findings: Source and negative controls are durably committed.
Version 2 is not proven to be invoked by any publication path.
No public artifact was implemented or deployed in this run.
repairs: Kept version 1 intact and treated version 2 as non-canonical until execution and integration evidence exist.
Blocked publication rather than inferring success from committed tests.
remaining_uncertainty: Runtime behavior under Node remains unverified.
No browser, mobile, accessibility, performance, privacy, or preview evidence exists for publication.
